rationale: Keeps parent 0003's residual-add + RMSNorm source byte-identical (same math, epsilon, two-kernel backward, process-local _COMPILED_KERNELS cache, autocast native fallback, num_warps=4, supported range) and appends a TP=1 fused cross entropy so the incremental effect is attributable. Forward: one row-wise Triton kernel over S*B rows with BLOCK=next_power_of_2(V) and a col<V mask for non-power-of-two V. Per row it loads logits into FP32 (masked lanes = -inf so they never win the max or contribute to sumexp), computes the row max M, Z=logits-M, exp(Z), sumexp, and loss = log(sumexp) - predicted, where predicted = Z at the target column guarded by (col==target)&mask so out-of-range labels (target<0 or target>=V, including -100 and lanes landing in [V,BLOCK)) contribute a zero predicted term and get loss=log(sumexp); they are NOT treated as ignore_index. It then overwrites the FP32 buffer in place with softmax P=exp(Z)/sumexp. Input mutation is explicit and native-exact: logits.float() returns the SAME tensor for FP32 input, so the observable forward mutation (input becomes P) is reproduced, while for float16/bfloat16 it allocates a separate FP32 copy and the original low-precision input stays exactly unchanged. No mark_dirty, exactly as native mutates its FP32 buffer in place without it; the autograd.Function saves P after the mutation so the saved-tensor version check passes, and the final-logits consumption scope is the same narrow one as native. Backward: one row-wise kernel reuses the saved probability storage as the gradient buffer (no extra [S,B,V] temporary, as native does), computing (P - onehot)*grad_output where onehot is set only at a valid in-range target ((col==target)&mask); out-of-range rows get plain softmax*grad_output with no class -1. The FP32 gradient is returned and autograd casts it back to the logits input dtype, matching native. V=1 degenerates correctly (loss 0, zero gradient at a correct single-class target). Both launchers reuse compiled code via the vendor CompiledKernel[(gx,gy,gz)] repeated-launch API keyed on device/V/block/pointer-alignment, pass only non-constexpr runtime args in order, and run on the current stream; the grid (rows) is a launch parameter so differing shapes reuse the same compiled kernel. No reshape/view/contiguous copies beyond a single contiguous() on the loss gradient, no tensor caching, no synchronization, and no imports beyond torch/triton. Performance is unverified; the CE fusion may remove many small aten launches, but the loop can correctly end in rejection if the complete-step wall-clock, current-best-normalized, no-regression or memory gates are not met.
